newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps fall, CFDs down 8 cts, mogas down $.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps fall, CFDs down 8 cts, mogas down $.

text.p: European oil swaps slipped on Monday , extending losses seen late last week.
Wet Brent remained under the cosh, trading at 48 cents under December the same as four trades done last week.

That trade was the equivalent of 20 cents under January which pressured CFDs for this week, forcing them 8 cents lower to 7 cents under January. The following three weeks were also softer but mostly dipped just a cent or two from late Friday levels.

Monthly Brent CFDs against the frontline IPE contract were well offered but there was little change in premiums. December asked 12 cents, January 25 cts and February 23 cts but buyers were difficult to find, said brokers.

Gasoline, which had shown occasional signs of strength last week, slipped $3.00 a tonne but activity was focused on physical barges where $220.00 a tonne traded a couple of times. Brokers pegged the balance of November at $216.00 and $207.50 for December.
Gas oil was little changed with swaps for physical holding at Friday"s levels and a slight widening of the first quarter crack spread versus Brent.

Swaps for 0.2 percent sulpur were slightly easier at $6.25 a tonne above the IPE for December with the first quarter holding at $7.50 above. The gas oil crack spread for the first quarter next year edged five cents a barrel wider to $5.35 a barrel but the next three quarters were unchanged at $4.45, $4.70 and $5.15 respectively.

Jet premiums were well bid after trade at $34.00 and $37.50 on December and January on Thursday last week. December was little changed but brokers pegged the first quarter slightly firmer at $38.00 or even slightly higher.

Heavy fuel swaps fell $2.00 a tonne from late Friday levels but activity was thin. Dealers said the underlying market was well supported, particualrly on low sulphur and in the Mediterranean. Barges remain dogged by good supplies of russian fuel which have been stored in Rotterdam by traders.

"The amount in storage is certainly not small and the bunker demand alone is just not enough," said a trader. December barges were around $115.00 and low sulphur at $128.00 but no trade was heard. -- Sam Arnold-Forster, London newsroom +44 171 542 4984
